q: How do you choose who you work with?
a: I look at six things: a credible business, a market you understand, an offer worth building on, customers worth winning, a team that responds and closes, and commitment to a long-term relationship. I read every application myself and say yes, not yet or no, with the reason.

q: What do you ask of me?
a: A credible business, honest numbers, a team that responds quickly and closes, and a long-term view. We set SMART goals together at the start. Every 10 weeks we review the results against them, and the numbers decide whether we scale up, change direction or scale down.

Before we start, we agree written criteria with you. A qualified opportunity is handed over only when the business fits your ideal customer profile, we have identified a decision-maker, there is evidence of a reason to talk now, and the reply has been reviewed and scored against those criteria. By default we score out of 100 and an opportunity needs 70 or more to be eligible. Opportunities that do not meet the bar are not handed over.

q: What happens if an opportunity is not right?
a: You tell us which opportunity and why. We review it against the criteria we agreed. Where it does not meet them, we replace it. We aim to keep replacements under 10 percent of handed-over opportunities, and we track that. The exact terms are set out in your written agreement.

Our partnerships are a monthly retainer that reflects the value of the opportunities we deliver, agreed once we have confirmed the fit. That only makes sense where winning the right customer creates enough gross profit and lifetime value to justify serious work to find them. We do not publish a price list on this website.

q: Why do you take so few partners?
a: Capacity is a performance decision. I keep LeadPipes deliberately small so I stay directly involved in every account, hold the quality standard, and avoid becoming an agency that wins clients faster than it can serve them. Each partner gets my time and a protected territory. When a category and state are taken, they are taken.

q: How do you find the people you contact, and is that compliant with the Spam Act?
a: We research businesses and contact people in their business capacity, using publicly published business contact details, and we record where each detail came from. Our messages are business-to-business, relevant to the person's role, identify LeadPipes, and include a working unsubscribe that we honour promptly. We design our outbound to comply with the Spam Act 2003 and Australian privacy law. We do not cold-contact consumers or homeowners. Details are in our privacy policy.

We do not guarantee sales or any particular result. We do not sell lists or shared leads. We do not cold-contact consumers. We do not run your sales conversation, proposal, close or delivery: that stays with your team.

q: Does the maths work for my business?
a: It works where winning the right customer creates enough gross profit and lifetime value to justify serious work to find them. LeadPipes is not built for a $300 transaction. In the application we ask about your average sale, gross margin, customer lifetime value, sales cycle and close rate so we can both see whether it adds up. If it does not, we will tell you plainly.
